messages:
Elena Park: Heads-up: eu-ingress is spiking with TLS validation errors after the IAM cleanup this morning. Seeing cert name mismatches and OCSP stapling missing.
Samir Patel: which IAM cleanup? PR or terraform apply id?
Elena Park: terraform apply tf-ops-2026-03-22 trimmed roles on serviceAccount:rotator-eu@infra -> removed cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.decrypt on the key version path.
audit-bot: ALERT: 12 KMS Decrypt DENIEDs (projects/eu/locations/global/keyRings/rotator/cryptoKeys/cert-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3) in last 10m
Jules (oncall): can you paste a sample proxy error and the audit log line? need to triage fast.
Elena Park: proxy log: `tls: certificate verification failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority for "api.eu.redwood"` then `rotator: failed to decrypt DEK: PermissionDenied`. pasted audit: `method=CryptoKeyVersions.Decrypt principal=serviceAccount:rotator-eu@infra status=PERMISSION_DENIED resource=projects/eu/locations/global/keyRings/rotator/cryptoKeys/cert-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3`
Samir Patel: hm, rotator fell back to cached cert bundle that was for staging hostnames. That caused client mismatch. Do we not validate fallback cert subject?
Elena Park: fallback path had weak checks. We added permissive fallback to reduce outage historically, but this time old cert had wrong CN.
Jules (oncall): mitigation: regrant Decrypt for that specific key/version and restart rotator; then disable fallback until we have stricter subject validation.
Samir Patel: agree. Also add a conditional IAM binding instead of broad re-add. I'll run a narrow grant: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/eu/locations/global/keyRings/rotator/cryptoKeys/cert-key --member=serviceAccount:rotator-eu@infra --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersionDecrypter --condition='expression=resource.name.endsWith("/cryptoKeyVersions/3")'`
infra-ci: CI: applying IAM change (change-id: iam-2026-03-22-02)
Elena Park: applied and restarted rotator pods (rotator-eu-2/rotator-eu-3). Observability: OCSP stapling restored for endpoints, handshake errors dropping to zero.
Jules (oncall): good. Root causes: 1) RBAC prune removed necessary key-version decrypt, 2) permissive fallback allowed mismatched cert to serve, 3) no automated IAM-to-service dependency tests.
Samir Patel: follow-ups: - add IAM impact smoke test that runs during TF apply and targets a matrix of services -> ensure key operations succeed - tighten rotator fallback: require subject SAN match and expiry grace threshold - enable KMS denied-rate alert correlated with tls.handshake_error - add canary job that validates OCSP stapling + TLS 1.3 + ALPN for each region's ingress every 10m
Elena Park: created infra ticket infra#6920 "rotator IAM preflight + fallback hardening" and started postmortem doc.
Jules (oncall): also document roll-forward vs rollback play: if IAM removal triggers DENIED > X, revert to last IAM snapshot. Add runbook entry for conditional grants and key-version scoping.
Samir Patel: long-term: consider envelope encryption with short-lived DEKs cached in rotator memory and signed attestations from KMS to reduce live KMS dependency at handshake. Also consider HSM-backed key for cert signing.
Elena Park: note for security: ensure KMS audit logs are shipped to SIEM with request payload hashes and include principal, methodName, resource name. We should be able to run forensic queries quickly.
infra-ci: NOTE: added TF plan check step to block role removals that are referenced by services via `infra/service-refs/*` map.
Jules (oncall): schedule: Samir to implement IAM smoke test, Elena to harden rotator fallback and add subject checks, I will update oncall runbook and add the revert snapshot step. Priya (not in thread) please review postmortem when ready.
Elena Park: will monitor for 30m. Last check +12m: no DENIEDs, OCSP stapling verified, client telemetry normal. Closing incident for now.
